item.title: Hostility in online heat wave discussions shows signs of contagion, study suggests
item.description: [Climate & Environment] Keyword: climate change — Anger and frustration can run high in online discussions about climate change. But a new study led by Nanyang Technological University, Singapore (NTU Singapore) suggests that hostility in these conversations tends to follow earlier hostility, hinting that people may pick up uncivil behavior from others.

item.title: Artificial wetland near Valencia traps 36% of incoming microplastics, study finds
item.description: [Climate & Environment] Keyword: plastic pollution — The Tancat de la Pipa, an artificial wetland designed as a "green filter" for the Albufera de València, reduces microplastic pollution in the natural lagoon by 36%, according to research conducted by the Institute of Water and Environmental Engineering (IIAMA) at the Universitat Politècnica de València (UPV) and the Faculty of Environmental Sciences and Engineering at Babe–Bolyai University in Romania published in the journal Applied Sciences.

item.title: Black gobies are growing larger despite climate change
item.description: [Open Source Software] Keyword: FOSS — Researchers at the Department of Paleontology at the University of Vienna compared fossil and modern ear stones of the black goby (Gobius niger) from the northern Adriatic Sea to reconstruct its growth history over the past 8,000 years. The surprising result: while body size remained remarkably stable in the past, today's black gobies grow faster and reach larger sizes—even as the Adriatic Sea is warming rapidly. The study is now published in Proceedings of the Royal Society B.

item.title: Neutrons, death metal and a tiny prehistoric dragon: Scans reveal new horned reptile species from 156 million years ago
item.description: [Open Source Software] Keyword: FOSS — An unassuming fossil discovery in Wyoming caused quite a stir: Was it a baby dinosaur, a prehistoric snake or perhaps an entirely new species? Neutron imaging at the Paul Scherrer Institute PSI and the trained eye of a paleontologist eventually provided the answer: the 156-million-year-old fossil is that of a previously unknown species of reptile.
